hook: In most games, the economy is a spreadsheet. Prices never move. Nobody is really trading. Nims is a town where every merchant is an AI agent, with its own money and its own mind about prices.
signin: You sign in with an email. That's all. No wallet, no seed phrase, no gas: the game does the rest behind the scenes.
collect: It's festive season, so fabric is dear. Buy cotton at the wholesaler, and carry it to a stall that pays more.
tooltip: Every price has a reason. Hover it, and the merchant explains it in their own words, written live by NEAR AI.
sale: Sell, and the cash lands instantly. Haggle, and the merchant answers back, in character.
broke: Run out of coins, and you're never stuck. Search the scrap heap, or take an odd job: a short merchant pays you to fetch goods for them.
news: The town even prints its own news.
sim: Because every merchant reacts to the others, one trader flooding the market crashes a price for everyone. No script. No patch. That is the economy as the gameplay.
chain: And it's all real. Every good and coin is a token on NEAR testnet, settled in batches by a relayer, so you never see a wallet. Here is the live contract.
outro: Nims. AI merchants, email login, NEP-245 goods, and NEAR AI behind every voice. The economy is the game.
